label: SOFR-IORB spread 12w vol-scaled
condition: buy pct_le 0.4 (2w, act +2w) | sell pct_ge 0.9 (2w) | between: hold
note: COMPUTED WEEKLY on same-day Friday spreads, each used from the Friday after (SOFR publishes the next morning), the freshest reading the tested weekly-bar construction allows -- one week. The screen's own rule ran a week older still: the research column is a week stale (its row for Sunday S is the spread of Friday S-9, matched on all 231 weeks) and the pipeline's ingest shifted it a further week, so the screen's transform at row S is built from the spread of S-16; with weekly_extra_lag_days 7 the feed reproduces its stored values to the last digit. FRESHNESS RUNS THE WRONG WAY on this rule, same percentile definition, same series: read a day fresh on daily bars it makes 0.4x to 0.7x against 2.7x buy and hold, on Friday bars a week fresh 2.2x to 2.5x against 2.4x to 2.7x, and as the screen tested it two weeks stale 3.3x to 3.7x. The extra week is off by instruction; that the edge lives in the staleness is on record and unexplained. The percentile is the screen's own definition, an expanding average-tie rank; on this series of ties the "share at or below" definition differs by up to 0.14. RULE, set 2026-09-16: TWO-SIDED. Long for 2 weeks when the percentile is at or below 0.40, short for 2 weeks when it is at or above 0.90, and between triggers keep the last side. ACTION DELAY: a buy trigger is traded two weeks after it fires, a sell trigger when seen; the band on the dashboard is the fresh reading, the position waits, and `pending` names the trade that has fired and not yet been placed. Chosen from a sweep of 105 delay and persistence cells (2023-10 to 2026-09, daily prices, buy and hold 2.23x): buy +2w / sell +0w is the peak at 7.46x, long-only 3.95x, and the ridge buy +1..3w by sell +0..2w is nine of nine cells at 3.1x or better, while delaying the sell past two weeks loses in every row and the daily feed needs about three weeks of delay on both sides to work at all. About twelve episodes; the peak is the best of correlated trials, the ridge is the evidence. Bands: buy to 0.40, good to 0.60, hold to 0.80, risk to 0.90, short from 0.90. READ ON FRIDAYS: on the same window the screen's own weekly percentiles make 4.2x against 2.6x buy and hold, the feed's Friday readings 2.4x, and daily re-checking 0.5x -- this one-basis-point series flips sides 48 times when read every day. Going flat between triggers scored the same (4.4x on the screen, 2.4x on the feed); a one-week short hold made no difference under keep-last-side. The earlier rule here (long at or below 0.20, short otherwise) made 3.2x and 1.7x on the same window; the screen's original row was pct_ge_90 Short / risk-off (1.20x, excess -1.8%). THE SERIES IS SOFR MINUS IORB, not the IORB rate: the research column named IORB is that spread (confirmed when the Pine port was matched to the Liquidity Stress Index ticker FRED:SOFR-FRED:IORB), and on the rate itself nothing fires -- a policy rate only moves at meetings. FRED serves both legs from 2021-07, so with the 52-week vol window and the 52-week percentile warmup the row is readable only from late 2023; the seed is the research column, snapped at 2dp, and the splice check confirms the construction. THE RESEARCH COLUMN IS A WEEK STALE: its row for the week ending Sunday S is the spread of Friday S-9, an exact match on all 231 weeks, like the Banks column. FRAGILE BY CONSTRUCTION: the spread moves in 1bp steps, and vol-scaling a 12-week change of a few bp makes the trigger depend on which day is sampled -- the same FRED spread run weekly on Thursdays and on Fridays agrees on only 43% of its own triggers. Watch item.
